33 An electric kettle is marked 3.10 kW. It is used with an electrical supply of 240 V.
What is the electric current in the kettle and what is the kettle’s electrical resistance when
working?
current / A
resistance / Ω
A
0.0129
18 600
B
0.0770
3100
C
12.9
18.6
D
12.9
3100

hints: Notice the kettle rating is $3.10\text{ kW}$, so first convert it to $3100\text{ W}$ before using it with the $240\text{ V}$ supply.
Connect power to current and voltage with $P = VI$, so the working current is $I = P/V$ for this kettle.
Then connect the same $240\text{ V}$ and your current to resistance with $V = IR$, or check with $R = V^2/P$.
walkthrough: Identify the working values: power $P = 3.10\text{ kW} = 3100\text{ W}$ and potential difference $V = 240\text{ V}$.
Use electrical power $P = VI$ rearranged to $I = P/V$ to find the working current.
Use $V = IR$ rearranged to $R = V/I$ for the hot working resistance, or equivalently $R = V^2/P$.
The pair $12.9\text{ A}$ and $18.6\,\Omega$ matches the table row. This is option C

A.explanation: Uses $3.10\text{ W}$ instead of $3100\text{ W}$, giving $I = 3.10/240$ and a resistance 1000 times too large.

B.explanation: Inverts $P = VI$ to $I = V/P = 240/3100$, giving about $0.0770\text{ A}$ instead of $P/V$.

C.explanation: Gives $I = P/V \approx 12.9\text{ A}$ and $R = V/I \approx 18.6\,\Omega$, consistent with $3.10\text{ kW}$ at $240\text{ V}$.

D.explanation: Current of $12.9\text{ A}$ is correct but $3100\,\Omega$ confuses the $3100\text{ W}$ power value with resistance.
